title: は — the topic marker
summary: は marks the topic of the sentence, the thing you are talking about: ‘As for ～, …’. It is written は but pronounced ‘wa’. It attaches to a noun and is used in the basic pattern A は B です.

patterns.gloss: A is B (私は学生です)
topic + は + comment (今日は天気がいいです)

body.p: Say what you will talk about, add は, then give the information: 私は学生です (As for me, I am a student). The topic is usually something both people already know.
As a particle, は is read ‘wa’, not ‘ha’. Elsewhere, such as in こんにちは, it also keeps its は spelling while being read ‘wa’.
In 今日は天気がいいです, the topic is 今日 and the comment is ‘the weather is good’. The comment has its own subject marked with が. This idea of topic first is basic to Japanese sentences.

examples.ja: 私（わたし）は学生（がくせい）です。
これはわたしのかばんです。
examples.romaji: Kore wa watashi no kaban desu.

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）は天気（てんき）がいいです。
examples.romaji: Kyō wa tenki ga ii desu.
examples.note: Topic 今日, then 天気が as the subject of the comment.

pitfalls: は is pronounced ‘wa’ but written は, not わ.
は marks the topic, not simply the doer. When you introduce new information, が is often used instead.
